Most of the tickets for "LOTERIA®" have been sold. The game is in the last part of its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, the top prizes are being claimed more slowly than the tickets are selling, which is a good sign.

Today's free summary of "LOTERIA®" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
959.headline: How much has sold

972.body:
"$8 Million Money Maker" offers a top prize of $8 million and eleven prize levels in all. The prize money leans toward small, frequent prizes. Games shaped like this pay out often, in small amounts. This design never changes, while every other number on this page does.

Every line of $8 Million Money Maker's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
972.headline: How this game pays out

975.body:
About two-thirds of the tickets for "$1,000,000 Money Rush" are sold. The top prize count has held, with two of four still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

Every line of $1,000,000 Money Rush's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
975.headline: Seven months, no top prize claimed

976.body:
"100X The Cash" paid out its last $2 million prize close to two months ago. The ticket still advertises it because printed tickets never change. Prize tables do change, and the biggest prize listed today is $10,000.

Everything above about "100X The Cash" comes from the North Carolina Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
976.headline: The advertised top prize is gone

980.body:

980.headline: What the prize table shows

If you play "50X The Cash" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
981.headline: Prize table details

985.body:
"MAX-A-MILLION" can match another game on price and top prize and still pay out very differently. This game is a game with most of its money in small, frequent prizes. Of its unclaimed prize money, most is in wins under $5,000 and the rest is in bigger prizes. Neither kind is better, and each suits different players.

If you play "MAX-A-MILLION" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
985.headline: Same price, different prizes

The numbers for "Emerald 10's" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
988.headline: What's actually left to win

990.body:
"LADY LUCK" is in the second half of its run, with about a quarter of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, a larger share of the top prizes is left than of the tickets, which is a good sign.

The numbers for "LADY LUCK" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
990.headline: How far along this game is

992.body:
"$2 MILLION VAULT" offers a top prize of $2 million and twelve prize levels in all. The prize money leans toward many smaller prizes. Games shaped like this pay small prizes often and large prizes rarely. This design never changes, while every other number on this page does.

The table below shows the full count for "$2 MILLION VAULT", with every prize level included.
992.headline: How this game pays out

993.body:
"$5,000 Triple Play" has gone six months without a top prize claim, and tickets kept selling. Only a fixed number of tickets are printed. About three-quarters of the tickets are sold, and every remaining $5,000 prize is still unclaimed. That leaves the same top prizes among fewer tickets.

Every line of $5,000 Triple Play's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.

"$1,000,000 Triple Play" is past the halfway point of its run, with about a third of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, the top prizes are being claimed more slowly than the tickets are selling, which is a good sign.
